Phenytoin NOT recommended for alcohol withdrawal SE - does not prevent withdrawal seizures
CIWA-Ar protocol after SE stabilized: symptom-triggered benzodiazepine dosing

output.summary: Alcohol withdrawal seizures: benzodiazepines are first-line, correcting GABA-A downregulation. Phenobarbital provides additive benefit via GABA-A positive allosteric modulation for refractory withdrawal SE. Phenytoin does not prevent alcohol withdrawal seizures and is not recommended for this indication. Thiamine deficiency encephalopathy: high-dose IV thiamine (500 mg TID for 3–5 days) is standard treatment (Prescott protocol). Electrolyte repletion — potassium, magnesium, phosphate — is critical in alcohol-related withdrawal management. CIWA-Ar symptom-triggered protocols reduce total benzodiazepine exposure after initial stabilisation.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Wilson is a 58-year-old man with severe chronic alcohol use disorder who is brought by ambulance in active status epilepticus. His neighbor, who checks on him regularly, called 911 when she found him convulsing on his front porch. She estimates she last saw him drinking 36 hours ago and that he had been trying to quit drinking this week after a conversation with his brother. He had no prior diagnosed epilepsy. He arrived by ambulance with continuous generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity for approximately 20 minutes. Paramedics noted multiple old bruises from probable falls. No IV access was obtained by EMS due to poor venous access — midazolam 10 mg IM was given without termination of seizures. He is a chronic heavy drinker with 10+ drinks daily for 20 years. He has a malnourished appearance. He has no prior epilepsy history.
